answer.rationale: memory_c2 documents that the low-cost vendor's onboarding was quick and invoicing stayed accurate, directly mitigating the two largest risks of a primary switch under a 14-day deadline. memory_c6 confirms that multi-year commitments unlock volume pricing, which I would use as a negotiating lever on the new contract rather than a constraint to avoid. The 18% cost-cut mandate is binding and the low-cost vendor's quote meets it alone; renewing the incumbent (memory_c1) or merely renegotiating (memory_c4) would preserve integration comfort but almost certainly fall short of the mandated reduction. A second-source action (memory_c3) is deferred because we have capacity for only one decision this cycle and the immediate contract expiry is the harder constraint. Delivery risk is bounded because memory_c2 shows the vendor's track record is clean, and the 94% line utilization—while tight—was not flagged in that record as having caused missed deliveries during the previous switch.
